rationale: The three-case experiment executed and was retained (CheckRun 0b99df9ed72e4cd2b653c5741e4eec3d, exit 0, tests_passed). It confirms the refined precondition by measurement: with TrailingLogs=0 the same legal history loops, while with TrailingLogs=10 or 25 the snapshot taken at index 4 compacts nothing because the log end had not yet outgrown the snapshot index, and the peer converges. This update records the measured interpretation, strengthens the precondition Behavior with the observed operands, and states explicitly that the earlier asserted results are unaffected because they ran with TrailingLogs=0.

knowledge.statement: compactLogsWithTrailing returns without deleting anything when lastLogIdx <= trailingLogs, and otherwise deletes up to maxLog = min(snapshotIndex, lastLogIdx - trailingLogs). Because a snapshot is taken at the FSM's applied index, a quiet cluster snapshots with snapshotIndex close to lastLogIdx, so the deletion stops below the snapshot index and the leader can still serve entries below its snapshot boundary. The boundary is compacted away only when lastLogIdx - trailingLogs >= snapshotIndex at the moment of the snapshot, i.e. when the log end is at least TrailingLogs ahead of the snapshot index when the snapshot is taken; TrailingLogs=0 satisfies this by construction. Measured in the three-case run: with TrailingLogs=0 the successor's store after its snapshot at index 4 was empty (first/last 0) and the peer looped; with TrailingLogs=10 or 25 the same snapshot left the store at 1..4, the later twenty entries extended it to 1..24, and the peer converged with no snapshot installs.
knowledge.conditions: Applies to any LogStore with a trailing-log configuration; the arithmetic is in compactLogsWithTrailing and the snapshot index is the FSM's applied index at snapshot time. Measured under: five bootstrapped nodes in one process, InmemTransport/InmemStore, two-sided partition of {leader, partner} from the other three peers, snapshot at index 4 with 0 or 20 post-snapshot entries, TrailingLogs in {0, 10, 25}, equal 1 s timeouts, frozen snapshot fd2d6988362c434e9fda87b87c5fb0df.
knowledge.changed_premise: Extended from source arithmetic to measured confirmation, and the earlier reading that a nonzero TrailingLogs merely delays the loop is corrected: a snapshot taken while the log end is only marginally ahead of the snapshot index compacts nothing at all, so the loop does not occur at any trailing value unless the log end has outgrown the snapshot index by at least TrailingLogs at snapshot time.

interpretations.rationale: The suspicion under test in this investigation was the generalisation that the snapshot-boundary loop occurs whenever a leader snapshots inside a rejoining follower's stale suffix, with a larger TrailingLogs merely delaying it. The retained receipt contradicts that reading, so the comparison is violated and that generalisation is refuted; the underlying defect remains asserted on its own, narrower basis. Parsed receipt CheckRun 0b99df9ed72e4cd2b653c5741e4eec3d, three cases of the same legal history: index 10 (TrailingLogs=0) rejoin_observe reports restores_before 0, restores_early 704, restores_late 715, partner_applied_index 4, partner_last_index 7, partner_store 5..7, successor_store 0/0, with the timeline at indices 4-9 rising 104, 219, 333, 458, 583, 704 and partner_applied_cmds fixed at 1; index 21 (TrailingLogs=10) reports restores 0 with partner_applied_index 24 and partner_last_index 24, and index 32 (TrailingLogs=25) the same, partner applied and last index 24. Indices 3 and 14/25 show why: after the snapshot at index 4 the successor's store was empty in the first case but 1..4 in the others, and the twenty post-snapshot entries left it at 1..24, i.e. no compaction reached the boundary. The arithmetic matches compactLogsWithTrailing: with lastLogIdx equal to the snapshot index at snapshot time, 4 <= 10 and 4 <= 25 make the function return without deleting, whereas TrailingLogs=0 lets the deletion reach index 4. Consequence for the record: the two asserted results (single-peer witness CheckRun 7772ad1b5b154d498a27a79806bb0ea7 and sealed-partition witness CheckRun f66fa4e4e0514f7e95b7788032144a30) are unaffected because both ran with TrailingLogs=0 and are scoped to that basis, but the claim must now be stated with its exact precondition: the loop requires the leader's log end to be at least TrailingLogs ahead of the snapshot index when the snapshot is taken, so the practical trigger is a snapshot taken while the applied index lags the log end by at least TrailingLogs (for example a user-triggered snapshot during a write backlog, or a threshold-triggered snapshot under sustained load), not a routine periodic snapshot in a caught-up cluster with default TrailingLogs.

knowledge.assertion: measured three-case confirmation and corrected reading of the trailing-log precondition

counterevidence: Both nonzero-TrailingLogs cases converged with zero snapshot installs and the peer reaching the leader's applied index 24, so compaction reaching the snapshot boundary is necessary for the loop, not incidental.
These cases and the earlier TrailingLogs=3 control are the same effect (no compaction at the boundary), not two independent protections.
limitations: The intermediate threshold was not bisected; only TrailingLogs in {0,10,25} with 0 or 20 post-snapshot entries was sampled.

The harness snapshots only through the user API at a quiet moment, so the threshold-triggered snapshot during a live write backlog - the configuration the narrowed precondition points at - was not executed.
Same in-process five-node setup throughout; no network transport and no default (10240) TrailingLogs sampling with a matching backlog.
interpretations.joint_history: Single receipt, three cases: indices 4-10, 15-21 and 26-32 come from one execution of the registered three-case experiment on the same frozen snapshot, each case a separate cluster built by the same harness, and every event carries trailing_logs so the cases are not conflated.
